name: purpose-built-human-male-left-foot-orthographic-v5
designConstraints: Exactly five relaxed toes, believable sole/arch/instep/heel/ankle; ordinary closed short ankle end in images. No pointed crown or calf shaft. Taper hidden ankle overlap after generation and measured uniform fitting only.

Six coherent orthographic views, shared isotropic scale and centered silhouette origin. Front/left/back/right at azimuth 0/90/180/270, top +90 elevation, sole -90 elevation. No rigid object tilt or diagonal foot references.
Reference coordinate toes -Y and left medial -X; actual source orientation must be inspected before proper rotation into stock +Y front and +X medial. Do not trust image labels alone.
Measure actual pmh0_footl001/lfoot_g and accepted shin. Stock width 122.5966 mm, length 297.6431 mm, height 163.2612 mm; stock sole -137.105 mm and crown +26.1562 mm relative to ankle pivot.
Initial 50K source with 2K maps, normal strength 1. The preceding same-raw 100K trial did not cure deformation; early untouched sole/top/underside anatomy gate precedes fitting or local edits.

Use soft directional light and restrained baked creases for texture definition; no hard cast shadows, false embossed anatomy or AO-as-height. Preserve exact source maps and separate controlled native AO/roughness descendants.
Exhaust proper rotation, positive uniform scale and placement. Preserve stock rig, attachments, animation, height, identity equipment and accepted six geometry/runtime dependencies.
Perfect one donor then mirror detached mesh only into opposite stock frame with correct winding and tangent handedness. Verify opposite-side seams and poses independently.

Offline feet-only collection. No NWN access in this task. Finish feet then await user; native/client bulk gates remain explicit. Future hands require nearly closed weapon-gripping pose, not authorization to start hands.
Freeze additive orthographic adapter and its exact upstream source dependencies; original live workflow is left unchanged. Camera support success alone does not prove a good reconstruction.
